title: GitHub Makes Agentic Workflows Generally Available with Isolation and Budget Controls
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-agentic-workflows-ga/en/headerimage/header-1793990975266.jpeg"/><p>GitHub Agentic Workflows is generally available, running coding agents in GitHub Actions with read-only defaults and separately scoped write jobs. Those protections do not cover direct write permissions or custom jobs, so they depend on how each workflow is configured.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: Presentation: Uncorking Queueing Bottlenecks with OpenTelemetry
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/opentelemetry-queue-observability/en/mediumimage/julian-oli-medium-1792652839179.jpg"/><p>Oli Lane and Julian Wreford share how Gearset replaced guesswork in distributed asynchronous queues with OpenTelemetry tracing. They explain why traditional metrics fall short, how to implement user-centric SLOs based on latency distributions, and share practical debugging tips to help senior developers, software architects, and engineering leaders improve system reliability and team culture.</p> <i>By Julian Wreford, Oli Lane</i>

title: Pinterest and Intel Take Open-Source Profiling to Internet Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/pinterest-intel-profiling/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793692423906.jpg"/><p>Pinterest has partnered with Intel to extend gProfiler, an open-source continuous profiler that provides production performance visibility across an internet-scale fleet of infrastructure.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Google Cloud Spend Caps Reach General Availability with API and Monthly Resets
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-cloud-spend-caps/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793609514337.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud has made spend caps on Cloud Billing Budgets generally available, pausing new usage of a service in a project once a monthly budget is hit, without deleting resources. GA adds an API, estimated live costs, and automatic monthly resets, but caps cover only the Gemini API, the Agent Platform, Cloud Run, and Cloud Run functions, and overages during enforcement delays are still billed.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Entire's Git Forge Rethinks Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/entire-git-forge-coding-agents/en/headerimage/entire-git-forge-agents-1794134163813.jpeg"/><p>Entire is a Git forge designed specifically for collaboration between human developers and AI coding agents. Its premise is that traditional software development infrastructure, particularly the pull request (PR) model, is not well suited to an environment where AI agents generate, review, and iterate on code at high speed.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Google Cloud Adds Self-Managed VMware Cloud Foundation on Bare Metal
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-cloud-self-managed-vmware/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793604325753.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud has made a self-managed VMware solution generally available, running VMware Cloud Foundation 9.x on dedicated Z3 bare metal with root access across ESXi, vCenter and NSX in 22 regions. It sits beside the Google-managed VMware Engine and matches customer-operated offerings from AWS and Oracle, shifting lifecycle, patching and Broadcom licensing back to the customer.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: GitLab 19.5 Makes Agentic Development a Governed Part of the DevOps Platform
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/gitlab-19-5-agentic-platform/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793095997884.jpg"/><p>GitLab 19.5, released on October 15, puts agentic software development and governance at the centre of the platform, making its GitLab MCP server generally available while expanding how external AI agents can interact with GitLab.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: AWS Ships Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-continuum-ga/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792886107294.jpg"/><p>AWS has made Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available in two regions. The service proves exploitability by running real exploits in a sandbox, then opens fixes as pull requests. Published pricing charges per finding processed as well as per line of code, and practitioners are asking what would justify letting it merge fixes on its own.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Vault Fork OpenBao Adds External Keys and Quantum-Ready TLS
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/vault-fork-openbao-27/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793734932785.jpg"/><p>OpenBao has released version 2.7, adding read scaling for PostgreSQL-backed deployments, support for external hardware security module (HSM) and key management service (KMS) keys, and post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. The release also introduces control groups for human review of sensitive operations and new headers intended to keep requests consistent across load-balanced OpenBao nodes.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: GitHub Actions Lockfiles Reach GA to Secure Workflow Dependencies
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-actions-lockfiles-ga/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793888107988.jpg"/><p>GitHub has made workflow dependency lockfiles for GitHub Actions generally available on October 28, 2026, two weeks after the feature entered public preview. Workflows can maintain clear tag and branch references.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Edera's Object Capability Bounded Authority Promises to Isolate Credentials from AI Agent Workloads
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/ai-credentials-isolation/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793853184587.jpg"/><p>Edera announced Object Capability Bounded Authority, a security model that separates an AI agent's or MCP server's required authority from the credentials behind it. Hypervisor-enforced capabilities limit agents to specific actions without storing secrets in the workload. Initial releases cover scoped command execution and workload identity; credential-brokered API access will follow.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Leapwork Play Reaches GA with Governance for Playwright Tests
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/leapwork-play-playwright/en/headerimage/header-1793826326573.jpeg"/><p>Leapwork Play adds requirement traceability and approval workflows around portable Playwright tests. Full governance and audit capabilities require an enterprise package.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: Presentation: Zero Trust Agent Systems that Pass Audits and Still Ship
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/zero-trust-ai-agents-production-security/en/mediumimage/advait-patel-medium-1792655207658.jpeg"/><p>Advait Patel shares a playbook for securing AI agent systems in production. He discusses moving defense boundaries from the prompt to the tool layer, enforcing scoped workload identities, and mitigating prompt injection via tool outputs. He explains how to structure audit-ready observability and implement kill switches to protect critical data while keeping deployment fast and compliant.</p> <i>By Advait Patel</i>

title: Amazon ECS Gateway Arrives with Generated Hostnames and No Custom Domain Support
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>AWS has released Amazon ECS Gateway, an account-level ingress resource letting platform teams define networking once and application teams opt services in with a connector. Each service gets a generated hostname and routing is host-based, and neither the announcement nor the documentation covers custom domains.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Docker Urges Isolation and Governance for AI Agent Security
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/docker-ai-agent-security/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793733720293.jpg"/><p>Docker has published a guide to five security risks that arise when AI agents are allowed to browse, run code and call tools with limited human oversight. They argue that the autonomy that makes agents useful also makes conventional application security controls insufficient. The company positions isolation and governance, rather than model improvements alone, as the main defences.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>
